setting: You four are parents of children on the same youth football team, and you all live in Chengdu, China. You know each other through the team: sidelines, pickups, and this group chat. You know roughly what each other does for work, but you are not close friends outside the team.
opener: Ask whether the team's Saturday session is still on for the kids.

Ming.knows: You know Jing is a pharmacist and that she is the one who keeps the team's first-aid kit stocked. You know Xiu runs admin at a hospital, and you've joked with her about needing a sick note. You know Yong dispatches taxis and always has the fastest route for a pickup.
Ming.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when the team needs something organised.

Jing.knows: You know Ming does freelance translation and that he's easy to reach when you need a document turned around. You know Xiu runs the hospital admin side and has been helpful with the team's medical forms. You know Yong drives a taxi and has offered lifts before.
Jing.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to pass on useful information.

Xiu.knows: You know Ming works as a translator from home and is usually free for calls. You know Jing is a pharmacist and has the team's first-aid supplies covered. You know Yong works for a taxi company and understands the city's traffic patterns well.
Xiu.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something needs a quick decision.

Yong.knows: You know Ming works from home as a translator and is often on the phone. You know Jing is a pharmacist and is good at keeping kids healthy in season. You know Xiu is a hospital administrator and has useful contacts for the team.
Yong.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to offer a lift or confirm a time.

private_lines.Ming: You work freelance as a translator from home, taking Chinese-English documents and manuscripts on deadline. You spend your days at a desk, with breaks for tea and errands, and you handle the school runs when your schedule allows. You live with no one in your flat, so you do the cooking and housework yourself.
private_lines.Jing: You work as a pharmacist at a neighbourhood pharmacy, on rotating shifts that include late evenings. Between work and home you manage the house and your child's training schedule. You live with no one, so you do most of the household chores yourself.
private_lines.Xiu: You are a hospital administrator, working set hours in an office and managing staff schedules and budgets. Your days are busy and structured, and you usually get home in the early evening. You live with no one, so you handle your own cooking and errands.
private_lines.Yong: You dispatch for a taxi company, coordinating drivers and handling calls from the office during early or late shifts. Your days revolve around the radio, the booking system, and keeping the drivers on schedule. You live with no one, so you manage your own meals and home.

situation: Parents of kids on the same football team.

text: Is the saturday session still on for the kids? I think the coach said something about the pitch
Not sure, nothing from the coach today. I can ask at pickup tomorrow
pitch is booked. 9am. saw the sheet this afternoon

on the radio all evening, can't look properly. ok
